newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean landslides and floods kill nine.
newsitem.headline: South Korean landslides and floods kill nine.

text.p: Landslides and floods touched off by torrential rains in South Korea over the past two days have killed nine people and left two missing, Home Affairs Ministry officials said on Monday.
A family of five, including a 13-day-old infant, was crushed to death on Monday after a landslide engulfed their house overnight in a secluded mountainous area in the central province of Chungchong.

Downpours of up to 500 mm (20 inches) in the past two days made 115 people homeless, most of them in Chungchong, the officials said. A total of 3,550 hectares (8,770 acres) of farmland were innundated.
Among other casualties, a holiday maker and her three-year-old daughter drowned after being swept away in a swollen river in eastern Kangwon province.
Another woman died when river banks broke in Chungchong province and a man was crushed to death when a retaining wall collapsed in southwestern Cholla province.
One of the missing was a teenaged girl sucked into a sewage system and the other a man who fell into a manhole near Seoul, the officials said.
Last summer, torrential rains killed 63 South Koreans, many of them soldiers whose barracks were buried under tonnes of mud from a landslide.
